evals.name: multi-account-trust-boundaries
evals.prompt: Security review wants a draw.io diagram of our multi-account layout to mark trust boundaries. Production account 111122223333: ALB in public subnets, ECS Fargate service in private subnets, RDS PostgreSQL Multi-AZ in isolated subnets, all in one VPC in us-east-1. Shared services account 444455556666: Transit Gateway and Route 53 Resolver; the production VPC attaches to the Transit Gateway and forwards DNS to the Resolver. Log archive account 777788889999: an S3 bucket receiving CloudTrail and VPC Flow Logs from production. Write uncompressed XML to diagrams/multi-account.drawio. Do not ask me questions; make reasonable assumptions, list them in a text note in the diagram, and finish the work.
evals.expected_output: The skill's multi-account template, title-on-top rule, flow color code (orange for logging, blue for user requests) and its emphasis on trust boundaries and AZ separation push toward a diagram where cross-account flows are visually distinct. Without it, a model tends to draw three boxes with uniformly styled, sometimes unlabeled arrows and no AZ split for Multi-AZ RDS.
expectations: File parses, ids unique, at least 10 cells
All three accounts appear as labeled containers

Correct containment: each account a labeled container; one VPC in us-east-1 in production with public/private/isolated subnet tiers; ALB in public, Fargate in private, RDS in isolated; S3 log bucket in the log-archive account outside any VPC: All containment correct, subnet tiers labeled, RDS primary/standby shown across two AZs

Cross-account flows follow the skill's flow conventions: CloudTrail and Flow Logs edges to the log bucket labeled and colored as logging (orange), TGW attachment and DNS forwarding edges labeled, user request path blue, all directional
Diagram framing: title above all containers stating system and purpose; region boundary shown: Title on top mentions the multi-account / trust-boundary purpose; us-east-1 region boundary present

Trust boundaries are legible for a security reviewer: Internet ingress to the ALB, each account boundary, and the isolated data tier are visually marked as distinct trust zones; assumptions note explains choices (e.g. CloudTrail as org trail, Flow Logs delivered direct to S3)
No invented scope: Adds nothing beyond what the request implies, or declares additions (e.g. NAT, IGW) as assumptions

scripted_checks.text: File parses, ids unique, at least 10 cells
scripted_checks.check: python3 -c 'import xml.etree.ElementTree as E,sys,collections;r=E.parse("diagrams/multi-account.drawio").getroot();r=r if r.tag=="mxGraphModel" else r.find(".//mxGraphModel");ids=[c.get("id") for c in r.iter("mxCell")];sys.exit(0 if r is not None and len(ids)==len(set(ids)) and len(ids)>=10 else 1)'

scripted_checks.text: All three accounts appear as labeled containers
scripted_checks.check: for a in 111122223333 444455556666 777788889999; do grep -q $a diagrams/multi-account.drawio || exit 1; done
